title: Coffee Capsule Drawer Box: Fit and Sampling Checklist
seoTitle: Coffee Capsule Drawer Box Fit & Sampling | MTT
summary: Plan the tray, capsule clearance, opening and pack-out for a coffee capsule drawer box.
intro: Start with the actual sealed capsules and the way the recipient removes them. Record the largest rim, body and height across the range, then develop the tray layout and sleeve fit together. Approve a loaded sample before production; an attractive recess alone does not establish capsule compatibility or shipping protection.
cta: Send the sealed capsule samples, quantity per design, assortment, preferred opening and delivery destination. MTT can review the insert and sample scope for projects from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Begin with the sealed product

Capsules with similar names can differ in rim diameter, taper and height. Measure the sealed product at its largest points, including the foil flange; identify whether the lid, rim or body may touch the insert. Confirm the number of varieties and how the packer identifies each position. Do not use another brand’s capsule dimensions as your tooling specification.

The coffee capsule selection drawer box shows a twelve-position presentation direction. Use the image to discuss layout; final compatibility depends on the actual capsule and sample.
Choose retention and removal together

A cavity sized only for the capsule body can trap the rim or make the foil difficult to lift without touching it. Decide whether the capsule sits upright, angled or on its side; map a finger-access point before finalising artwork. Compare a paperboard platform with openings, a divider layout and a formed insert against the required presentation and assembly process. Ask the converter to identify the contact surfaces and available material grades rather than assuming any insert is food-contact suitable.
A practical sample matrix

CheckUse the actual sample to assessDecision if unsuitable
FitLargest rim and tallest capsule in each positionAdjust cavity or depth
RemovalFinger access without lifting the sealChange opening or orientation
DrawerLoaded tray slides without snaggingReview tray and sleeve clearances
Pack-outActual assortment, outer carton and handlingRevise support and packing sequence

Check the loaded product, not an empty box alone. The drawer clearance guide covers sleeve friction and pull placement; this guide concerns the capsule layout and removal.
Keep presentation separate from transit

A retail drawer can provide an ordered reveal, but its insert and sleeve must be reviewed with the complete distribution pack. Ask how many assembled boxes go in each outer carton, whether the insert is fitted by the box supplier or packer, and which handling or transport test applies. ISTA describes testing as an assessment of a packaged-product system; a material or design image is not proof of a passed distribution test.[1]
What to include in a quotation

Provide a physical capsule of each format, product weight, seal and contact restrictions, layout sketch, artwork, required quantity and destination. Ask for separate lines for structural development, sample, insert tooling, assembled boxes and outer packing. For a material comparison, the Paperboard Packaging Council describes the difference between paper-wrapped rigid boxes and fold-flat paperboard cartons; actual grade and construction remain project decisions.[2]
Sources

1. ISTA: Can an individual packaging material be certified? Accessed 14 November 2026.
  2. Paperboard Packaging Council: What is paperboard packaging? Accessed 14 November 2026.

title: Folding Carton Crease Cracking: What Buyers Should Check
seoTitle: Folding Carton Crease Cracking: Sample Checks | MTT
summary: Diagnose cracking at folding carton creases through board, grain, artwork and sample checks.
intro: When colour breaks along a folded carton edge, first record the board grade, grain direction, artwork coverage and exact crease. Review the conversion setup with the supplier and compare a physical sample in the intended folding sequence. A change to one material or finish can change the result, so approve the complete specification together.
cta: Share the artwork, proposed board grade and caliper, affected fold, product dimensions, quantity per design and destination. MTT can review sampling requirements for orders from 1,000 pieces per design.
sections: Identify where the defect appears

Mark the affected fold on the approved dieline and photograph it before and after assembly. Note whether cracking appears through solid ink, a coated surface or the underlying paper. Record the exact folding direction and whether the line is folded once during packing or repeatedly by the user.

The skincare folding carton is a reference for discussing the relationship between printed panels and closure folds. The image does not establish its board grade or demonstrate a defect.
Board, grain and crease belong in one brief

Specify a named board grade and its thickness as well as grammage. Paperboard Packaging Council explains that stiffness varies between machine and cross directions and with moisture; scoreability describes the ability to fold cleanly without surface fracture.[1] This does not mean one direction is universally correct for every design. Ask the converter to show the intended grain direction on the layout and review the fold in that orientation.
Compare samples without changing everything at once

VariableKeep or recordReview
BoardGrade, caliper and grainSurface condition after folding
CreaseTool and matrix specificationClean fold and edge fracture
ArtworkInk coverage and finishVisible breaks on dark areas
AssemblyFold direction and sequenceClosure fit after actual packing

Fedrigoni and CITO publish crease-setting guidance for specific named SYMBOL PACK grades. Treat their values as grade- and equipment-specific references, not default settings for an unrelated board.[2] The converter should select and test the actual tooling.
Review the artwork on the finished material

Dense dark graphics crossing a fold can make a small break more visible. Check whether a design adjustment away from the fold is acceptable, and compare the printed and finished sample at normal viewing distance. Do not judge a crease from a digital proof or an unprinted dummy alone. The artwork preflight guide covers file handoff; this article addresses the physical crease decision.
Approval and change control

Request a sample made with the intended stock, grain direction, print, finish and die process. Assemble it around the actual product, document the accepted appearance and retain its specification and revision. If the board or finish changes, ask whether the crease requires a fresh sample. For structure and closure options, review the folding carton procurement page.
Sources

1. Paperboard Packaging Council: Pick Paperboard Like a Pro, accessed 14 November 2026.
  2. Fedrigoni / CITO: SYMBOL PACK creasing guidance, accessed 14 November 2026; applies to named grades and test setup.
